title: Input symbol read from its wire
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over Booleans, let $n,s$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a Boolean string of length $n$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$. For any input-head position $p$, if the input-head position in the encoding of $c$ is $p$, then the Boolean symbol obtained by reading the encoded input wire at $p$ (with boundary positions yielding no symbol) equals the symbol scanned by $c$ on its input tape.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
the encoded input-head position of $c$ equals $p$
